title: Bank ledger
intro: You are writing the core of a toy bank. Transactions arrive as a list of dicts already in chronological order. Use only the standard library. Each level extends the previous one.
rules: `type` is either "deposit" or "withdraw"; `amount` is a whole number of dollars.
Accounts start at balance 0 the first time they appear.

levels.title: Apply transactions to balances
levels.prompt: Write `balances(tx)` that applies every transaction and returns a dict of account -> final balance. Deposits add, withdrawals subtract. At this level do not check anything: a balance may go negative and amounts are assumed valid.

levels.title: Reject overdrafts with a reason
levels.prompt: Write `apply(tx)` that returns `(balances, rejected)`. A transaction is rejected, and does not change any balance, when its amount is not positive (reason `"invalid amount"`) or when a withdrawal is larger than the account's current balance (reason `"insufficient funds (balance B, needed N)"` with the real numbers). `rejected` is a list of `(id, reason)` tuples in input order. A rejected transaction must not create the account.
levels.signature: def apply(tx: list[dict]) -> tuple[dict[str, int], list[tuple[int, str]]]
edgeCases: A withdrawal equal to the balance is allowed
Check the amount before the balance

levels.title: Monthly statement per account
levels.prompt: Write `statement(tx, account, month)` where month looks like `"2026-02"`. Use the Level 2 rules to decide which transactions count. Return a dict with `opening` (the balance before the month starts), `lines` (a list of `(date, type, amount, balance_after)` tuples for the accepted transactions of that account in that month, in order) and `closing` (the balance after the last line, or `opening` when the month has no lines). Rejected transactions never appear in `lines`.
levels.signature: def statement(tx: list[dict], account: str, month: str) -> dict
edgeCases: A month with no activity returns opening == closing and lines == []
